Chad's whole crude output was 46.2 million barrels in 2020 (USGS).

panguna-mine-bougainville.whole: From 1972 to 1989 Panguna produced about 3.1 million tonnes of copper and 306 tonnes of gold, about 2.5% of world copper output. Its metals were worth K15,100 million, 44% of Papua New Guinea's exports over the period, and its dividends, taxes and royalties came to about 17% of the country's internally generated revenue (C.K. Brooks, c. 1991). A Harvard Growth Lab dispatch gives 45% of exports and 17% of tax revenue. In 1973 the government's share of the company's A$158.4 million net profit was about A$29 million; the company paid no income tax for its first three years, and the royalty was 1.25% (ANU Press).

costa-rica-2021-public-wage-freeze-emplo.whole: By the IMF's figures, central government debt fell from 67.6% of GDP in 2021 to 61.1% in 2023, the primary balance moved from a deficit of 0.3% of GDP in 2021 to surpluses of 2.1% in 2022 and 1.6% in 2023, and growth was 7.9%, 4.6% and 5.1% in 2021–23; the IMF paid out all of the roughly US$1.6 billion and called fiscal performance strong (IMF, June 2024). El Financiero found the education ministry budget fell 12.7% after inflation over the five years to 2024, and social investment fell from 11.8% of GDP in 2022 to a planned 9.7% in the 2024 budget (November 2023). The head of the judicial investigation police told Interferencia there had been over 300 departures since 2018, against seven resignations in 2011–17 (cited by El Financiero).

kenya-1991-university-fees-esac.whole: The credit agreement made release of each tranche conditional on keeping new public university intake to no more than 10,300 in 1992/93 and 10,600 in 1993/94, and capping student loans at KSh 21,500 (IDA credit agreement, 1991). A later study found that in 1994 the government still bore up to 92% of university costs and households as little as 8%; loan recovery was 3.3% when the Higher Education Loans Board was set up in 1995 and over 18% by 2000–01; public university enrolment grew more than 400% between 1987 and 2000 while government funding rose about 30% (Otieno, 2004). The same study found the richest fifth of households supplied 45% of university students and the poorest fifth 8% (1994 data).

turkey-january-1980-price-rises-sal.whole: Inflation (GDP deflator) fell from 104% in 1980 to 42% in 1981 and 28% in 1982; exports rose from US$2.9 billion in 1980 to US$4.7 billion in 1981 and US$5.7 billion in 1982; GDP shrank 1.1% in 1980 and grew 4.2% and 4.5% in the next two years; the current-account deficit narrowed from US$5.6 billion in 1980 to US$3.2 billion in 1982 (Anne Krueger, NBER, 1995). A 1984 MERIP analysis by Altan Yalpat reported that loss of purchasing power continued after 1981 wage rises and the wage share of national income fell; official unemployment rose from 15.4% in 1980 to 18.2% in 1982 (a figure the author called highly dubious), accumulated external debt was estimated at US$23 billion, and Iran, Iraq and Libya accounted for 65% of the 1981 export rise.

ghana-1987-1988-school-feeding-boarding-.whole: The World Bank's own evaluation department reviewed all Bank support to Ghana's basic education from 1986, across five projects including this credit, so its figures are not specific to this credit. It found the Bank financed about 8,000 classroom blocks and 35 million textbooks over 15 years, and literacy among 15–24-year-olds rose from 49% to 68% between 1988 and 2003 (World Bank OED, 2004). It also found teaching methods were not affected by the Bank's work, plans to extend in-service teacher training were not carried out, and schools in poorer, off-road rural areas were left behind. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.

angola-april-2024-diesel-price-rise.whole: World Bank economists put Angola's fuel subsidies at 3.7% of GDP in 2023 (World Bank blog, May 2025). After the April 2024 rise, the finance ministry reported fuel-subsidy spending of 588.8 billion kwanzas in the second quarter of 2024, 18% below the first quarter but 137% above the second quarter of 2023 (Lusa/VerAngola). Expansão, using finance ministry data, calculated fuel subsidies cost about 9.1 trillion kwanzas from 2021 to mid-2024, against about 6.3 trillion for health and education together. Diesel rose again, from 200 to 300 kwanzas a litre, in March 2025; the IMF estimated that move could free up US$3 billion (Daba Finance).

barrick-pascua-lama-estrecho.whole: Pascua-Lama never reached production. It was planned to yield 800,000–850,000 ounces of gold and 35 million ounces of silver a year in its first five years, at a capital cost of over US$8 billion, but was on hold from 2013, and in September 2020 a Chilean environmental court ordered its closure (MINING.COM, 2020). In June 2013 Barrick said it expected write-downs of US$4.5–5.5 billion and no production before mid-2016 (MINING.COM, 2013). Barrick also agreed to pay US$140 million to settle a US class action accusing it of distorting facts about the project.
